text:
alex: small convo: can we standardize how we expose semantic error categories in headers? we keep seeing customer confusion between throttling (client should retry), quota (contact billing), and model-degraded (failover to cheaper model).

priya: Totally. Customers parse 429 today and assume retry; but sometimes it's quota and retry just wastes cycles. I think headers are the least breaking path.

sam: proposal: `X-RW-Err-Cat: throttle|quota|billing|degraded|internal` and `X-RW-Err-Intent: retry|giveup|fallback|escalate`

mira: We'll also need to add console badges: little pill that says `quota` or `throttle` on the request sample. helps support triage.

alex: Telemetry: emit `client_error_class` label with `cat` and `intent` so dashboards can filter. Also include `client_version` where available.

priya: For rollouts that change semantics, can we have an `X-RW-Err-Ver: 2026-03-29.v2` to let SDKs detect contract changes and call registered callbacks?

sam: yes. Console UX idea: when a route has mixed error versions observed, show "in transition" banner with % of traffic per version. Clicking shows mapping rules and a link to the RFC.

mira: Edgecase: CDNs and proxies often strip unknown headers. we should fall back to encoding a compact JSON blob in the body under `error_meta` for clients behind proxies. Keep it small.

deploy-bot: deploy: feature/error-headers rolled to canary (10%) on prod.

alex: Next steps: priya to write compatibility table mapping current codes to categories; mira to draft console mock; sam to add telemetry event `error_version_observed` and counts. We'll sync tomorrow. :calendar:
